businessType: Direct-to-consumer brand selling premium home/wellness products online. ~45 employees. Revenue driven by paid social and search acquisition plus repeat purchases from an existing customer base. Founded 2020.
stage: $8.0M trailing revenue, 35% YoY growth (from $5.9M). Blended gross margin 60%. Marketing spend grew from ~$1.2M to ~$2.6M YoY. Blended CAC rose from ~$38 to ~$61 per new customer. 12-month repeat-purchase rate fell from 42% (2022 cohort) to 28% (2024 cohort). Average order value roughly flat at ~$72.
ownerGoal: Hit $12M revenue next year by roughly doubling paid acquisition spend again, then raise a growth round on the back of the growth rate.
ownerConstraints: Cash constraint: ~$1.4M cash, ~9 months runway at current burn; the doubling of ad spend assumes either reinvested margin or a new raise.
Inventory constraint: working capital is tied up in inventory; faster growth increases inventory financing needs.
Channel constraint: ~80% of new customers come from two paid platforms whose CPMs have risen; founder is reluctant to diversify channels mid-scale.
Brand constraint: founder believes brand momentum and growth rate are the fundraising story and does not want to slow spend.
Data constraint: analytics show blended CAC and a cohort repeat-purchase table, but contribution margin per cohort (after CAC, COGS, shipping, returns) has not been calculated.
immediateConcern: Founder framing: 'We just grew 35% to $8M and the brand is on fire. The plan is simple - double down on paid acquisition, hit $12M next year, and raise on the growth story. Growth solves everything. CAC ticked up a bit but that is just the cost of scaling, and revenue is clearly outrunning it. I do not want to take the foot off the gas to overthink the numbers.'
